ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\cos B= \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$, $\sin C= \frac{3}{5}$, and $AC= \frac{5}{3}$. What is the area of $\triangle ABC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: Draw AD$\perp$BC at point D through point A,\\
$\because$ $\sin C=\frac{3}{5}$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{AD}{AC}=\frac{3}{5}$,\\
$\therefore$ AD=$\frac{3}{5}AC=\frac{3}{5}\times\frac{5}{3}=1$,\\
$\therefore$ CD=$\sqrt{AC^{2}-AD^{2}}=\sqrt{\left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^{2}-1^{2}}=\frac{4}{3}$,\\
$\because$ $\cos B=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle B=45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ BD=AD=1,\\
$\therefore$ BC=BD+CD=1+$\frac{4}{3}=\frac{7}{3}$,\\
$\therefore$ The area of $\triangle ABC$=$\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{7}{3}\times1=\boxed{\frac{7}{6}}$.

$\because$ $\sin C=\frac{3}{5}$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{AD}{AC}=\frac{3}{5}$,\\
$\therefore$ AD=$\frac{3}{5}AC=\frac{3}{5}\times\frac{5}{3}=1$,\\
$\therefore$ CD=$\sqrt{AC^{2}-AD^{2}}=\sqrt{\left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^{2}-1^{2}}=\frac{4}{3}$,\\
$\because$ $\cos B=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle B=45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ BD=AD=1,\\
$\therefore$ BC=BD+CD=1+$\frac{4}{3}=\frac{7}{3}$,\\
$\therefore$ The area of $\triangle ABC$=$\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{7}{3}\times1=\boxed{\frac{7}{6}}$

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\cos B=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$, $\sin C=\frac{3}{5}$, and $AC=\frac{5}{3}$. What is the area of $\triangle ABC$?
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution}: Draw AD$\perp$BC at point D through point A,\\ $\because$ $\sin C=\frac{3}{5}$,\\ $\therefore$ $\frac{AD}{AC}=\frac{3}{5}$,\\ $\therefore$ AD=$\frac{3}{5}AC=\frac{3}{5}\times\frac{5}{3}=1$,\\ $\therefore$ CD=$\sqrt{AC^{2}-AD^{2}}=\sqrt{\left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^{2}-1^{2}}=\frac{4}{3}$,\\ $\because$ $\cos B=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$,\\ $\therefore$ $\angle B=45^\circ$,\\ $\therefore$ BD=AD=1,\\ $\therefore$ BC=BD+CD=1+$\frac{4}{3}=\frac{7}{3}$,\\ $\therefore$ The area of $\triangle ABC$=$\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{7}{3}\times1=\boxed{\frac{7}{6}}$
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, A is above, BC is the approximately horizontal base, B is on the left, C is on the right, therefore when drawing perpendicular AD from A to BC, the foot of the perpendicular D is located inside BC, and can serve as the height of the triangle. Reasoning: Draw AD perpendicular to BC. In right triangle ACD, sin C = AD/AC = 3/5, and AC = 5/3, so AD = (3/5)(5/3) = 1. By the Pythagorean theorem, CD = sqrt((5/3)^2 - 1^2) = sqrt(25/9 - 9/9) = 4/3. Also cos B = sqrt(2)/2, so angle B = 45°. In right triangle ABD, angle D = 90°, angle B = 45°, therefore it is an isosceles right triangle, BD = AD = 1. So BC = BD + CD = 1 + 4/3 = 7/3. The area of triangle ABC = (1/2) × BC × AD = (1/2) × (7/3) × 1 = 7/6.
